zh.title: 曝光三角：先把高光保住
zh.summary: 快门、光圈、ISO 不是三个平等旋钮。先定运动，再定景深，最后才用 ISO 救场。

zh.title: 灯比：先学 ratio，再学灯位
zh.summary: 一盏主灯加一块反光板，已经能拍出大部分人物场景。先控制亮暗差，再追求灯位花样。

zh.title: 构图：先让观众知道看哪里
zh.summary: 观众第一眼该看谁，第二眼该看哪，构图就是排这个顺序。先定主体，再管前中后景。

zh.title: 一扇窗怎么当主光
zh.summary: 没有灯组也能拍人脸：先定朝向，再用反光板补一点，最后把背景压下去。

zh.title: 越轴之后，观众会突然找不到方向
zh.summary: 两个人对话，摄影机跨到桌子另一边，观众会以为他们换了位置。先定一条线，再决定要不要跨。

zh.title: 拍摄清单写到别人能替你执行
zh.summary: 清单要写清楚先拍什么、拍多久、拍不到怎么办。想拍的都写上去，现场反而没法执行。

zh.title: B-roll：让那句话有画面
zh.summary: 受访者说“每天早上五点出摊”，画面还停在脸上，观众就只能听。B-roll 要把这句话变成看得见的东西。

zh.title: 运镜：先问为什么动，再问怎么动
zh.summary: 镜头动起来不难，难的是让观众不觉得摄影机在炫耀。动之前先写清楚：观众要跟着谁、发现什么、被什么压住。

zh.title: 房间先开口：用场景交代人物
zh.summary: 人物还没说话，观众已经在读房间：门口有没有鞋、桌上几只杯子、哪盏灯还亮着。场景不是背景，是第一句台词。

zh.title: 场记：每条拍完，都得能接上
zh.summary: 场记不是记时间码。他记的是观众会不会发现：杯子换了手、外套扣错了、太阳突然从另一边来。现场多写一行，剪的时候少找一天。

zh.title: 机位高度：蹲下比换镜头有用
zh.summary: 同一张脸，机位高一寸，观众就读成另一个人。高度先决定权力关系，再决定景别；换镜头解决不了站错位置。

zh.title: 焦距：先决定观众站多远
zh.summary: 广角不是装得下，长焦不是拍得远。焦距先决定观众离人物多远，再决定脸和背景怎么挤。先走位，再换镜头。

zh.title: 景别：观众该看见多少
zh.summary: 景别不是远景、中景、特写的名词表。它决定观众和人物的距离：看见他站在哪，还是只看见一个眼神。先问这一刀要观众看什么，再决定机位退到哪儿。

zh.title: 走位：让人用身体说话
zh.summary: 走位不是把演员摆好看，而是让身体在空间里做出关系：谁靠近、谁退、谁挡住谁。

zh.title: 覆盖：别只拍一个角度
zh.summary: 覆盖不是多拍几条，而是给剪辑留下能救场的不同信息：全景、近景、插入、反打。

zh.title: 传感器尺寸：画幅决定什么
zh.summary: 传感器尺寸改变的是视角、景深和低光，不是“电影感”本身。

zh.title: 波形图：看曝光，不靠感觉
zh.summary: 波形图看亮度分布，不看画面好不好看；先保高光，再决定暗部留多少。

zh.title: 灯光风格：柔、硬、自然
zh.summary: 灯光风格先选一个方向：柔、硬、自然；三个都要，画面就会没有态度。

zh.title: 现场安全：电线、高处、道路
zh.summary: 现场安全先看三样：电线会不会绊人、高处有没有固定、道路有没有车。

zh.title: 帧率：动作与慢动作
zh.summary: 帧率决定动作的时间感；升格不是慢，是让观众看清一个瞬间。

zh.title: 快门角度：运动模糊
zh.summary: 快门角度控制运动模糊；180 度是常态，不是唯一答案。

zh.title: ND 滤镜：白天大光圈怎么拍
zh.summary: ND 滤镜不是压暗画面，是让白天也能开大光圈、保住景深。

zh.title: 伪色：一眼看高光
zh.summary: 伪色把亮度分成色块，一眼就能看到脸是不是过曝、天空是不是死了。

zh.title: Log 素材：拍的时候想后期
zh.summary: Log 不是“灰片更好看”，它把高光和暗部留给后期，前提是曝光和色彩管理做对。

zh.title: 夜景内景：一盏 practical 怎么撑
zh.summary: 夜景内景先找画面里能信的实用光，再用一盏小灯补人脸，别把整间房打平。

zh.title: 混合光：两种色温别打平
zh.summary: 混合光不要全部打成白；保留窗光冷、灯泡暖，空间才有层次。

zh.title: 硬光：影子也是构图
zh.summary: 硬光不是“难看”，它用影子划分空间；问题通常出在影子落错地方。

zh.title: 实用光：画面里的灯怎么用
zh.summary: 画面里的灯要真的亮、真的灭、真的闪，但它照不亮整张脸，只能当动机。

zh.title: 无线领夹：藏麦与备份
zh.summary: 领夹麦先解决藏和备份：衣领下、头发里、胶带固定，再录一条备用轨。

zh.title: 吊杆操作：跟着动作走
zh.summary: 吊杆跟着动作走，不跟着台词走；台词会停，身体不会。

zh.title: 双系统录音：合板不靠猜
zh.summary: 双系统录音要么拍手合板，要么时间码同步；两样都没有，后期只能猜。

zh.title: 手持：让呼吸进画面
zh.summary: 手持不是乱晃，是把摄影师的呼吸变成节奏；先稳住脚步，再谈晃动。

zh.title: 稳定器：走路的节奏
zh.summary: 稳定器最怕碎步；膝盖微屈、脚跟着地、速度均匀，画面才会稳。

zh.title: 陈设：用道具说人物
zh.summary: 陈设不是买一堆好看的东西，而是让每件道具回答“这个人为什么把它留在这里”。

zh.title: 道具连贯：杯子放在哪
zh.summary: 道具连贯靠照片：开机前拍桌面、拍手、拍衣服，收工前再拍一次。

zh.title: 多机位同步：时间码与机位图
zh.summary: 多机位先画机位图，再对时间码；剪辑要知道哪台机器站在哪。

zh.title: LED 虚拟拍摄：先对跟踪，再对光
zh.summary: LED 虚拟拍摄先对跟踪，再对光；跟踪漂了，再漂亮的背景也贴不住。

zh.title: 直播编码：码率、推流、备份
zh.summary: 直播编码先算上行带宽，再定码率；永远留一条本地录制备份。

zh.title: 拍摄许可：公园、地铁、商铺
zh.summary: 拍摄许可不是一张纸，它决定你能不能架灯、挡路、拍到招牌。

zh.title: 风险评估：开机前填一张表
zh.summary: 风险评估一页纸：谁可能受伤、什么会掉、出了事谁负责、最近的医院在哪。

zh.title: 多机位与直播：先把时间码、返送和录制锁死
zh.summary: 多机位不是多摆两台机器，而是让三台机器进同一条时间线、同一套返送、同一份录音。任何一个环节没有备份，现场就会从“导播”变成“猜”。

zh.title: LED 虚拟拍摄：墙、跟踪、同步与色温
zh.summary: LED 虚拟拍摄不是“背景换成屏幕”。它把真实光影、相机跟踪、屏幕刷新和后期色彩绑成一条链；任何一项没锁，演员脸上的光就会和背景分开。

zh.title: 现场硬光：硬、混、实用
zh.summary: 硬光不是缺点；问题是硬光、实用光和色温三种来源有没有被安排在同一张脸上。

zh.title: 声音吊杆：双系统、无线、杆操
zh.summary: 现场声音的可靠性来自双系统、无线备份和杆操位置，不是某一个贵麦克风。

zh.title: 运镜：手持、稳定器、覆盖
zh.summary: 运镜不是让画面动起来，而是让运动服务走位、覆盖和剪辑点。

zh.title: 多机位：同步、覆盖、走位
zh.summary: 多机位不是多开几台机器；同步、景别分工和走位重复，缺一个就剪不起来。

zh.title: Log 与曝光：波形、假色、ND
zh.summary: Log 不是万能；曝光、ND 和假色要一起定，否则后期只剩一张灰片。

zh.title: 现场安全：风险评估、许可、收工
zh.summary: 现场安全不是一张签字表；风险评估、许可和收工检查要落到每一个会动的人。

zh.title: 访谈布光：窗光、单灯与混合光
zh.summary: 访谈布光不是把脸打亮，是让人敢说、让剪辑有反应；先定方向，再定比例，最后才加灯。

zh.title: 低照度拍摄：噪点、快门与实用光
zh.summary: 夜景不是把 ISO 拉高，而是先决定哪些黑可以接受，再用实用光和快门换回细节。

en.title: The Exposure Triangle: Protect the Highlights First
en.summary: Shutter, aperture, and ISO are not three equal knobs. Set motion first, depth second, and use ISO last.

en.title: Lighting Ratio: Learn the Ratio Before the Positions
en.summary: One key and one reflector can shoot most portrait scenes. Control the contrast first, then collect positions.

en.title: Composition: Tell the Eye Where to Look
en.summary: Who should the eye hit first, and where does it go second? Composition is that order. Set the subject, then the layers.

en.title: How to Use One Window as Your Key Light
en.summary: You do not need a lighting kit for a face: set the direction, add a little bounce, then bring the background down.

en.title: Cross the Line and the Room Disappears
en.summary: Move the camera to the other side of a conversation and the audience thinks the people swapped seats. Pick a line before you cross it.

en.title: Write a Shot List Someone Else Can Run
en.summary: A shot list says what comes first, how long it takes, and what happens if it fails. A wish list says everything at once.

en.title: B-roll: Give the Sentence a Picture
en.summary: When someone says “I set up at five every morning” and the camera stays on their face, the audience can only listen. B-roll turns that line into something visible.

en.title: Camera Movement: Ask Why Before How
en.summary: Moving the camera is easy. Keeping the audience from noticing the machine is the work. Write down what they should follow, discover, or feel before you move.

en.title: Let the Room Speak First
en.summary: Before anyone speaks, the room is already talking: shoes at the door, two cups on the table, one lamp left on. Set dressing is the first line.

en.title: Continuity: Every Take Has to Cut
en.summary: Continuity is not timecode. It is what the audience will notice: a cup switching hands, a button undone, sunlight jumping to the other side. One extra note on set saves a day in the edit.

en.title: Camera Height: Lower Before You Change Lenses
en.summary: The same face at one inch lower reads as a different person. Height sets the power relationship before the shot size; a new lens cannot fix standing in the wrong place.

en.title: Focal Length: Decide How Close the Audience Stands
en.summary: Wide is not “fit everything in,” and long is not “shoot far away.” Focal length decides how close the audience stands before it decides how the face and background stack. Walk the scene first, then change the lens.

en.title: Shot Size: Decide How Much the Audience Sees
en.summary: Shot size is not a vocabulary list of wide, medium, and close. It sets the distance between the audience and the person: do they see where he stands, or only an eye? Ask what this cut needs before moving the camera back.

en.title: Blocking: Let the Body Tell the Story
en.summary: Blocking is not pretty placement; it makes relationships visible in space: who approaches, who retreats, who blocks whom.

en.title: Coverage: Do Not Shoot One Angle
en.summary: Coverage is not more takes; it gives the edit different information: wide, close, insert, reverse.

en.title: Sensor Size: What the Frame Really Changes
en.summary: Sensor size changes angle, depth, and low light, not "cinematic feel" by itself.

en.title: Waveform: Exposure You Can Measure
en.summary: The waveform measures brightness, not beauty. Protect highlights first, then decide how much shadow to keep.

en.title: Lighting Style: Soft, Hard, Natural
en.summary: Pick one direction first: soft, hard, or natural. All three at once means no attitude.

en.title: Set Safety: Cables, Heights, Roads
en.summary: Cables, heights, traffic: check those three before anything else on set.

en.title: Frame Rate: Motion and Slow Motion
en.summary: Frame rate sets how motion feels; high speed does not slow time, it lets the eye study a moment.

en.title: Shutter Angle: The Amount of Blur
en.summary: Shutter angle controls motion blur. 180 degrees is a default, not a rule.

en.title: ND Filter: Wide Open in Daylight
en.summary: An ND filter does not darken a picture; it lets you stay wide open in daylight and keep your depth.

en.title: False Color: Find the Clip at a Glance
en.summary: False color turns brightness into bands, so clipped skin or a dead sky is obvious at a glance.

en.title: Log Footage: Shoot for the Grade
en.summary: Log is not "flat looks pro"; it preserves highlights and shadows for post, if exposure and color are handled.

en.title: Night Interior: One Practical Can Carry a Room
en.summary: Find a practical light the room can believe, then add one small face light. Do not flatten the whole room.

en.title: Mixed Light: Keep the Two Temperatures
en.summary: Do not white-balance mixed light into one color; keep the cool window and warm bulb for depth.

en.title: Hard Light: The Shadow Is the Shape
en.summary: Hard light is not ugly; shadows shape the space. The problem is usually that the shadow lands in the wrong place.

en.title: Practical Light: Use the Lamp in the Frame
en.summary: A lamp in frame must actually turn on, off, or flicker, but it motivates light rather than lighting the face.

en.title: Wireless Lav: Hide It, Back It Up
en.summary: Hide the lav, secure it, and record a backup track before worrying about brand.

en.title: Boom Operator: Follow the Action, Not the Line
en.summary: The boom follows action, not lines. Lines stop; bodies keep moving.

en.title: Dual-System Sound: Slate and Timecode
en.summary: Sync dual-system sound with a clap or timecode. With neither, post is guessing.

en.title: Handheld: Let Breathing Into the Frame
en.summary: Handheld is not random shake; it turns the operator's breath into rhythm. Steady the feet first.

en.title: Stabilizer: Walk Like You Mean It
en.summary: Gimbals hate tiny steps. Soft knees, heel-first, even speed.

en.title: Set Dressing: Props Tell the Character
en.summary: Set dressing is not shopping for pretty objects; each prop answers why this person kept it.

en.title: Prop Continuity: Photograph the Table
en.summary: Continuity lives in photos: shoot the table, hands, and wardrobe before and after the take.

en.title: Multicam Sync: Timecode and a Camera Map
en.summary: Draw the camera map, then sync timecode. The edit must know which camera stood where.

en.title: LED Volume: Track First, Light Second
en.summary: In LED volume work, lock tracking before lighting. If tracking drifts, no background will stick.

en.title: Live Encoding: Bitrate, Uplink, Backup
en.summary: Calculate uplink before bitrate, and always keep a local recording as backup.

en.title: Permits: Parks, Transit, Shops
en.summary: A permit is not paper; it decides whether you can stand a light, block a walkway, or frame a sign.

en.title: Risk Assessment: Fill One Page Before You Roll
en.summary: One page before rolling: who can get hurt, what can fall, who is in charge, and where the nearest hospital is.

en.title: Multicam and Live: Lock Timecode, Return, and Recording First
en.summary: Multicam is not more cameras. It is three cameras on one timeline, one return, and one audio plan. If any link lacks a backup, directing turns into guessing.

en.title: LED Virtual Production: Wall, Tracking, Sync, and Color
en.summary: LED virtual production is not swapping a backdrop for a screen. It binds practical light, camera tracking, panel refresh, and color into one chain; if one link is loose, the light on the actor separates from the background.

en.title: Hard light on location: hard, mixed, practical
en.summary: Hard light is not a defect; the question is whether hard, practical and colour are arranged on the same face.

en.title: Sound rig: dual system, wireless, boom
en.summary: Reliable location sound comes from dual system, wireless backup and boom position, not one expensive mic.

en.title: Camera move: handheld, stabiliser, coverage
en.summary: Camera movement is not motion for its own sake; it serves blocking, coverage and the cut.

en.title: Multicam: sync, coverage, blocking
en.summary: Multicam is not more cameras; sync, shot-size division and repeatable blocking make it editable.

en.title: Log and exposure: waveform, false colour, ND
en.summary: Log is not magic; exposure, ND and false colour must be decided together or post gets flat grey.

en.title: Set safety: risk, permit, wrap
en.summary: Set safety is not a signature; risk, permit and wrap checks must reach every moving person.

en.title: Interview Lighting: Window, Single Lamp, Mixed Light
en.summary: Interview lighting is not about brightening a face. It makes the subject willing to talk and gives the edit reactions; set direction first, then ratio, then add lamps.

en.title: Low-Light Shooting: Noise, Shutter, Practicals
en.summary: Low light is not about raising ISO. Decide which blacks can stay black, then use practicals and shutter to buy back detail.
